utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, how long did those civilians stay in that school building?

utterances.speaker: ENES RIBIC
utterances.text: I would say for a brief period of time. For them it probably appeared much longer. I would say it was seven to ten days. I didn't keep a diary of course, but I would say that the time, for me, passed by fairly quickly. I can't say exactly how long they were there for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a physician yourself, did you learn of a woman on occasion who were in the sports hall during her sojourn there lost 30 kilogrammes of weight while she was there?

utterances.speaker: ENES RIBIC
utterances.text: That is ludicrous and medically untenable, that for such a short space of time you could lose 30 kilogrammes anywhere. That's not logical and I didn't hear of anything like that happening, I must admit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, did you happen to learn that there was some captured members of the HVO who were not put up in the sports hall but they were accommodated somewhere else, held somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: ENES RIBIC
utterances.text: I must say that next to my clinic, some ten metres away from my clinic there was some premises. I don't know how to describe them or define them. They belonged to the forestry administration. And I did see some people there through the window from time to time. So this was in the neighbouring building. I saw some people through the window. I didn't know who they were. I didn't know that they were incarcerated there. In fact I didn't know who they were. So I can't say whether they were members of the HVO or not. But I did see some, not many, but maybe five or six people, in those premises. They seemed to be shut in there. But I don't know who they belonged to. They weren't wearing uniforms. I just saw their heads, if the truth be told. I was walking underneath the window. I was chopping wood underneath the window, so I could communicate with them. But I didn't actually do so. And they didn't talk to me either, although they saw me there. As I say, I was underneath their window chopping wood. That's something I did on a fairly regular basis, in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, while the people were there, did you ever happen to notice that somebody was abusing those people, mistreating them? Did you learn anything about that from somebody else, that somebody was mistreating those people?

utterances.speaker: ENES RIBIC
utterances.text: No, never. I never learned anything like that. I never even heard people shouting at them. I can't say categorically, but -- and they're small windows, you know, the type of window you would find on a garage. I never ever heard any screams or moans or anything like that. No, that was out of the question. I would have reacted myself had I heard anything like that taking place. I would have gone and seen what that was all about, if anybody was mistreating people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Ribic, tell me please: After these events, did you ever happen to learn that when these people were being brought in from Maline, for example, that something happened which would -- which shocked you especially?

utterances.speaker: ENES RIBIC
utterances.text: I don't follow your question. Could you repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the fact that these people were brought to the school building, did you ever learn that when they were brought in an event took place which was talked about later on and which shattered the people?

utterances.speaker: ENES RIBIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately I did hear that during the conflicts a certain number of people were killed in the conflicts, and that some of them, as I say, were killed even if they lived through the conflicts; that some were killed during the conflicts, some of them survived the conflict but were killed later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear who killed them?

utterances.speaker: ENES RIBIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately I heard that they were killed by - how shall I put it - the people we mentioned earlier on, the mujahedin, and foreign fighters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Mr. President, for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. The other counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. In view of the time, I think that it would be a good idea to adjourn there for the day. Unless you have a question, Mr. Mundis, one question perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think I would prefer to start tomorrow morning, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Doctor, we're going to continue tomorrow when the Prosecution will be asking you questions. The Defence took an hour in examining you. I assume that the Prosecution will have one hour of questioning, and then perhaps the Defence counsel will have more questions to ask you and I'm sure that the Judges will have some questions for you. You will be going back to where you're staying and please come back tomorrow morning at 9.00. Between now and then, you are to have no contacts with the Defence counsel or the Prosecution. We are now -- you are now a witness of justice, so you should not contact anybody. I'm going to ask Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom, and you will be taken over by the Victims and Witnesses Unit. So we see you back here tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the few minutes that remain, I turn to the Defence as regards tomorrow's planning and schedule. When we complete the testimony of this witness, what do you have in store for us tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have another witness tomorrow Enes Karic [sic] and after that we have Ferid Jasarevic, the next witness, and Mustafa Hockic. And he could begin on Wednesday and be completed by Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. The name is Munir Karic. I don't know what I said; it seems I misspoke and gave a different name. The witness's name is Munir Karic. So I apologise for giving the wrong name. A slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If I understand you correctly, we have this particular -- the witness we started plus another witness. On Wednesday we have one more witness, and on Thursday a witness. Thank you. So we adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of November, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
